title: Framing is preserved outside scratch addresses
statement: Let $W$ be a word size, let $Z$ specify a layout with $F$ local variables per frame and stack bound $Q$, and let $\sigma$ be a state with local values $\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)$ and memory values $\sigma_{\mathrm{mem}}(a)$. Suppose a memory map $m$ stores the encoded constants $1,0,-1$ at their designated addresses, stores each pool index $n\le Z.\mathrm{disp}$ at its pool address, stores the stack address for frame pointer $q$ at the frame-pointer address, and stores $\sigma_{\mathrm{loc}}(x)$ at stack address $q+x$ for every $x<F$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{mem}}(a)$ at address $a$ for every $a<Z.\mathrm{lim}.\mathrm{space}$; also suppose $1\le q$ and $q+F\le Q$. If $m'$ agrees with $m$ outside the scratch addresses (the addresses $-21,-15,-17,-19,-13$, and $-(23+4j)$ for $0\le j\le 2F$), then $m'$ satisfies the same storage and frame-bound conditions for $Z,\sigma,q$.
hypotheses_covered: Agreement of $m'$ and $m$ outside the specified scratch-address set
